Swell windows HELD at their stored arcs and optimal_swell_dir: the ray-cast does not write these spots. Applied by pipeline/sw1_raycast.py (_apply_raycast_result, mode=full) and by pipeline/enrich.py (Algo 2a, after the ray-cast or the carried-forward arcs), so neither a full ray-cast nor a re-enrich moves them. Each entry is the window the spot carried on main when the hold was set (2026-10-19, main 7839cc0), copied verbatim; nothing here is authored.

WHY THESE TEN. The R1-R3 island rules (pipeline/enrichment/swell_window.py) judge each island on its own run of rays, so the Bimini group (1-23 km2 at 90-114 km) no longer borrows Cuba's run 600-700 km behind it, and on the land data alone every one of these spots would open its south-east gap (run 18: Hillsboro Beach [17-127, 145-175] -> [17-175]). The land data is not the whole obstacle here: the Great Bahama Bank is a shallow platform a few metres deep that breaks and refracts swell long before it reaches the islands GSHHG draws, so it shelters south-east Florida more than its islands do. Until that sheltering is measured (NWPS or the answer key), these spots keep the windows they had.

TO RELEASE A SPOT, delete its entry; the next full ray-cast writes its R1-R3 window. Keys are slugs as pipeline/db_import._slugify makes them; `name` is for the reader and is checked against the roster by pipeline/tests/test_swell_window_holds.py.
note: SE Florida, Hillsboro Beach to Hobe Beach: the Great Bahama Bank's shallow water shelters more than the land data shows.
